key_insight: A fixed-frequency four-transmon lattice-patch architecture can serve as a surface-code-friendly building block while achieving high-fidelity CNOT gates in all connectivity directions.
engineering_relevance: The design reduces frequency-crowding and mapping overhead compared with conventional qubit-coupler-qubit layouts, making it a promising hardware primitive for scalable fault-tolerant quantum processors.
method: Couple four fixed-frequency transmons to one fixed-frequency coupler in a lattice-patch arrangement.
Map the patch directly onto a surface-code plaquette to simplify logical-qubit compilation.
Use virtual Rz phase updates to correct residual phases from cross-resonance driving.
evidence_signal: Multi-level simulations report CNOT gate fidelities above 0.98 across all six connectivity directions in the patch.
watch_item: Cross-resonance driving introduces residual phase accumulation, so careful calibration is required to maintain gate fidelity.
paper_title: Lattice patch structure for fixed-frequency transmon quantum computer with high-fidelity CNOT gates
